questions.stem: A converging (convex) lens has a focal length of 10 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. Which type of image is formed?
questions.explanation: When the object is beyond 2F (twice the focal length = 20 cm), a converging lens produces a real, inverted, diminished image. At 30 cm, the object is at 3F, well beyond 2F. Using the lens equation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/10 - 1/30 = 2/30, so v = 15 cm. Since v (15 cm) < u (30 cm), the image is diminished. Option A describes what happens when the object is closer than the focal point.

questions.stem: A person who is long-sighted (hyperopia) has difficulty seeing nearby objects clearly. Which type of lens is used to correct this?
questions.explanation: Long-sightedness occurs when the eye lens cannot refract light enough to focus on the retina for nearby objects — the focal point falls behind the retina. A converging (convex) lens adds extra convergence, bringing the focal point forward onto the retina. A diverging lens (option A) is used for short-sightedness, where the focal point falls in front of the retina.

questions.stem: A magnifying glass is a converging lens. To produce a magnified, upright image, where must the object be placed?

options.text: Between the lens and the focal point (closer than F)

questions.explanation: When an object is placed between a converging lens and its focal point, the lens produces a virtual, upright, magnified image — this is how a magnifying glass works. At the focal point (option B), parallel rays emerge and no clear image is formed. Beyond 2F (option A), the image is real, inverted, and diminished. At 2F (option D), the image is real, inverted, and the same size.

questions.stem: A diverging (concave) lens always produces images that are:
questions.explanation: A diverging lens always produces virtual, upright, and diminished images, regardless of where the object is placed. The light rays spread out (diverge) after passing through the lens, so they never converge to form a real image. The image appears to be on the same side as the object and is always smaller than the object.

questions.stem: A camera uses a converging lens with a focal length of 50 mm to photograph a building 100 m away. Where does the image form relative to the lens?

options.text: Exactly at the focal point (50 mm behind the lens)
Very close to but just beyond the focal point

questions.explanation: For very distant objects, the incoming light rays are nearly parallel, so the image forms very close to the focal point. Using the lens formula: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/0.05 - 1/100 = 20 - 0.01 = 19.99, so v = 0.05003 m, which is just slightly beyond 50 mm. Option A is almost correct but the image is technically just beyond F, not exactly at F (that would only be true for an object at infinity). Option C confuses object distance with image distance.
